summary: Single-author proposal that human-LLM conversation histories be treated as an auditable artifact ('LLMography', by analogy with a bibliography). A prototype (FastAPI plus an unspecified OpenAI model) reads a pasted transcript and outputs LLM-estimated KPIs (Prompt Quality, Human Direction, AI Dependency, Auditability, Traceability, Privacy Risk) and a label from A to E. The 'evaluation' averages these LLM outputs over 19 engineering-student conversations, with no human ground truth, and applies the framework to the author's own writing of the paper.

claims.claim: Students' interactions were mostly human-AI co-produced, averaging 86.8 Human Direction, 81.9 Prompt Quality, 72.8 Auditability and 77.1 Traceability
claims.evidence: Tables 3-4 and App. A. All scores are generated by the LLM analyzer, and §6.7 states there is no comparison with human-coded ground truth. The scores are internally inconsistent: single-turn conversation C09 gets Traceability 0, while single-turn C10 gets Traceability 100 and Auditability 90.

claims.claim: Traces with command logs, file inspection and explicit artifacts are more auditable
claims.evidence: Qualitative statement in §6.5, based on the same unvalidated LLM scores; no analysis is shown.

claims.claim: The paper's own writing process was human-originated, human-directed and AI-assisted (Label B)
claims.evidence: Table 5: the author scores their own ChatGPT conversation; it is not stated whether the prototype produced these numbers.

claims.claim: AI transparency should move from output detection to documenting interaction history
claims.evidence: A position. No comparison with detection or with plain prompt logging is made.

patterns.note: Conversation transcripts as an audit artifact, with derived indicators. Not validated against any ground truth.
Proposes 'Human Direction' and 'AI Dependency' indicators that could in principle monitor over-reliance. No comprehension, learning, or skill outcome is measured.
An LLM scores the conversations, with no inter-rater or human agreement figures.

methodology.sample: 19 student conversation reports (462 turns; three are single-turn); one self-application
methodology.models: Unspecified OpenAI model inside the prototype
methodology.languages: n/a (LaTeX, UML/BPMN, report writing, some backend code)

standards.peer_review: Not peer-reviewed; the comment calls it a 'preliminary exploratory study'
standards.artifacts: None. The prototype, analyzer prompt and data are not released
standards.preregistration: none; consent was oral, and the paper says written consent 'should be' completed later

biases.detail: Every reported number is an LLM estimate; there is no human coding.
The author applies their own framework to their own manuscript and reports high scores.
Volunteers who agreed to have their AI use audited.
Renames prompt logging and provenance (W3C PROV) as a new '-graphy'.

coi.detail: No vendor affiliation, but the author's own tool is the only system evaluated, and the author's own writing is used as a showcase.

verdict_reason: There is no validated measurement. All KPIs are unvalidated LLM outputs on 19 conversations, with visible scoring inconsistencies, nothing is released, and the 'case study' is the author grading their own paper. It is a concept note, not evidence.
applicability: Does not transfer as evidence. The only usable idea is a design prompt: link agent session transcripts to the commits they produced, so reviewers can see who decided what. Do not use LLM-scored 'human direction' or 'AI dependency' numbers to judge a developer's reliance or comprehension; this paper gives no basis for their validity.
